extracted.intended_audience: mammalogists, taxonomists, systematists, and zoologists interested in rodent supraspecific classification
extracted.subtask_description: Diagnosing and distinguishing genera and subgenera of chipmunks (Eutamias, Neotamias, Tamias) using osteological, dental, muscular, and pelage characters; provides comparative morphological criteria and geographic context for supraspecific classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of the malleus
rubrics_metrics.description: The malleus is composed of a head and neck, a manubrium with a spatulate process, a muscular process, an articular facet spiraling halfway around the head, and a lamina joining the tympanic bulla; in Eutamias the head is not elongated and the plane of the lamina makes approximately a 90 degree angle with the plane of the manubrium, whereas in Tamias the head is elongated and the angle is approximately 60 degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures 1-3 illustrate differences. Variation: slight individual and age variation, no secondary sexual variation; intraspecific size variation in Neotamias. Asiatic Eutamias mallei may resemble Neotamias. Use malleus morphology as a diagnostic supraspecific character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of the baculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacula among sciurids fall into six structural types; in Eutamias the baculum is broad at the base, tapers to a tip with a dorsal keel and tip upturned in an even curve; in Neotamias it resembles a leg and foot with a narrow central keel and dorsally curving tip; in Tamias it is slender, nearly straight, upturned at the tip and has a ventral keel on the tip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare to figures 4-10 and to Pocock (1923) descriptions. The author classifies bacula of Nearctic sciurids into diagnostic groups and uses baculum structure as a key supraspecific character. Note individual and age variation; interspecific variation exists but general plan remains constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of the hyoid apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyoid made of arched basihyal with thyrohyals, hypohyal attached by ligaments, ceratohyal posteriorly, and stylohyal ligament; in Eutamias the hypohyal and ceratohyal are fused in adults, while in Tamias they remain distinct throughout life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissections of hyoid musculature support differences; related feature: conjoining tendon of anterior/posterior digastric muscles ribbonlike in Eutamias vs rodlike/rounded in Tamias. Use fusion state of bones and muscle/tendon cross-section as diagnostic characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence or absence of P3 and projection of anterior root of P4
rubrics_metrics.description: Eutamias normally has P3 present and the anterior root of P4 projects buccally (outside) of the masseteric knob; Tamias normally lacks P3 and the anterior root of P4 projects to the lingual side or directly to the masseteric knob.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P3 may be vestigial or variable in some specimens; rare exceptions occur (e.g., a Tamias specimen with P3 present but P4 projection still lingual). Some authors regard P3 presence as of minor generic significance, but the author argues dental formula changes are fundamentally significant. Use presence/absence together with P4 projection for generic diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of tail relative to total length
rubrics_metrics.description: In Eutamias the tail is more than 40% of the total length; in Tamias the tail is less than 38% of the total length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative metric useful for distinguishing genera; note ecological comparisons (Tamias resembles Spermophilus in this trait). Measure total length consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color pattern (longitudinal stripe configuration)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Eutamias the widths of longitudinal stripes are uniform (subequal) and only the two lateralmost dark stripes are short; in Tamias the dorsal longitudinal light stripes are more than twice as wide as the other stripes and all four lateral dark stripes are short.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color pattern varies little across chipmunks but is diagnostic in combination with other features. Eutamias dorsalis is aberrant but still characteristic. Use stripe width, which stripes are short, and presence of median dark stripe (present in both) as characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape of the infraorbital foramen
rubrics_metrics.description: In Eutamias and Tamias the infraorbital foramen is rounded; in most species of Neotamias it is slitlike (subovate to rounded in some Neotamias; E. townsendii is rounded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variation exists within Neotamias (e.g., E. townsendii). Use shape (rounded vs slitlike/subovate) as a distinguishing character but check for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Width of postorbital process at base
rubrics_metrics.description: The postorbital process is broader at the base in Eutamias and Tamias than in most species of Neotamias; E. townsendii may have a relatively broad base like Eutamias/Tamias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative breadth (base width relative to process length) is the metric; there is gradation in Neotamias. Use comparatively rather than absolute measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position of supraorbital notch relative to posterior notch of zygomatic plate
rubrics_metrics.description: In Eutamias and Tamias the supraorbital notch is distinctly anterior to the posterior notch of the zygomatic plate; in Neotamias the supraorbital notch is even with or slightly posterior to the posterior notch of the zygomatic plate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This difference may correlate with overall skull size (heterogonic growth). Consider size effects when using this character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of convergence of upper tooth-rows
rubrics_metrics.description: Rows of upper cheek-teeth converge posteriorly in Eutamias and Tamias (though some E. sibiricus asiaticus are nearly parallel); in most Neotamias the rows are nearly parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine posterior convergence visually or by measurement; note exceptions in some species (E. townsendii). Use in combination with other dental and cranial characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of constriction of interorbital region
rubrics_metrics.description: The interorbital region is more constricted in most Neotamias than in Eutamias and Tamias; some Neotamias (E. t. townsendii) approximate the constriction seen in Eutamias/Tamias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of constriction correlates with skull size; assess relative constriction rather than absolute distance. Use alongside other cranial metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape of the pinna (external ear)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pinna is narrower and more pointed in Neotamias, whereas in Eutamias and Tamias the pinna is broad and rounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External ear shape is a consistent field character; include pelage/ear morphology in diagnosis. Exceptions/gradation exist; corroborate with skeletal characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance in cross section of conjoining tendon of digastric muscles
rubrics_metrics.description: The conjoining tendon of the anterior and posterior pairs of digastric muscles is ribbonlike (flattened) in Eutamias and rodlike (rounded in cross section) in Tamias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissection required; use as a muscular character supporting hyoid apparatus differences. Consider preservation and preparation effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lambdoidal crest development
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of development of the lambdoidal crest varies: least developed in Neotamias and most developed in Tamias; degree of development increases with skull size and is likely an expression of heterogonic growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as size-related (allometric) feature rather than a primary phylogenetic character. Use cautiously and consider skull size/ontogeny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters too weakly expressed to be of taxonomic use
rubrics_metrics.description: The following features are judged too slight in expression or too variable within groups to be relied on taxonomically: (1) degree of posterior projection of the palate; (2) relative size of the auditory bullae; (3) position, in relation to P4, of the notch in the posterior edge of the zygomatic plate; (4) size of m3 in relation to m2; (5) degree of development of the mesoconid and ectolophid of the lower molars; (6) shape and length of the rostrum; (7) degree of distinctness of minute longitudinal grooves on the upper incisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author explicitly recommends no reliance on these characters because of slight expression or marked variation. They are listed to caution against their use as supraspecific diagnostic criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite diagnostic syndrome (genus/subgenus diagnoses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnosis strings combining multiple characters (skull lightness, postorbital process weak, infraorbital foramen lacking canal and relatively large, presence/absence of P3, malleus/head angle, hyoid bone fusion, tendon cross-section, baculum keel position, tail % of total length, stripe arrangement) are used to define genera Eutamias and Tamias and subgenera Eutamias and Neotamias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple characters in combination (an integrated syndrome) rather than a single trait to assign supraspecific rank. The paper provides full formal diagnoses for Genus Eutamias, Subgenus Eutamias, Subgenus Neotamias, and Genus Tamias to be applied as taxonomic keys.
